title: A Letter for the Witness
premise: Ada Quintana, a night-shift dispatcher who has spent twelve years quietly cataloguing the town of Marrow Creek's secrets through its taxi bookings, receives an advance payment from a nervous stranger who asks her to prove a murder that hasn't happened yet — and then he turns up dead, exactly as the file he left behind predicted. Following the stranger's coded instructions, Ada discovers the killer is someone with access to the police case files, someone who has been rehearsing the murder for months through her own dispatch logs. As Ada races to decode the file and trap the killer, she realizes the final entry names her. In the end, Ada uses her twelve years of archived knowledge to turn the killer's own meticulous record against him, choosing to expose the town's complicity — and her own — rather than protect it, and finally claims a place in Marrow Creek not as its silent keeper but as its witness.
about_author: Lena Hartwell is a former emergency dispatcher who spent a decade answering calls in small industrial towns before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about the people who keep a community's records — and its secrets.

chapters.title: The Night Rate
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A slow night shift at Marrow Creek Taxi establishes Ada's ritual: logging every ride, every odd request, twelve years of the town's hidden rhythms. A man named Elias Voss arrives at midnight and pays triple in advance for a single job: prove that a murder scheduled for Friday hasn't happened. The beat is quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Voss refuses to say whose murder, leaving only a manila envelope: a partial case file, pages redacted in someone's careful hand. Ada wants to hand it to the police but notices the file contains details only she could know — her own dispatch logs. The emotional beat: professional pride curdling into violation.

chapters.title: Friday, 2:14 A.M.
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She spends two nights cross-checking bookings against the file and finds a pattern of rides that map a rehearsal: the killer has been practicing the route. Friday comes; Ada stays awake, watching her board. At 2:14 a.m. a cab is booked to Hollow Bridge Road. The beat: helpless anticipation snapping into alarm.

chapters.title: Hollow Bridge
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She reaches the bridge first and finds not a body but Voss, alive, waiting — then he is struck by a car that vanishes before she can see the plate. He dies murmuring 'check the return trips.' The beat: guilt and terror; the murder she was paid to prevent has happened, just not the one she expected.

chapters.title: The Return Trips
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Grieving and suspected by the police, Ada deciphers Voss's clue: the killer always books a return ride twenty minutes after each 'practice' run. She finds six return trips over three months, all from the same unlisted number. Beat: grief transmuted into methodical resolve.

chapters.title: Detective Reyes
chapters.summary: Detective Marisol Reyes's POV, first appearance. Reyes works Voss's murder and pegs Ada as either witness or accomplice. Reyes reveals Voss was a former police records clerk fired for 'irregularities' — meaning he had legitimate access to case files, and so did whoever fired him. Beat: wary, adversarial alliance forming.

chapters.title: What the Town Files Away
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Flashbacks woven through: twelve years ago Ada came to Marrow Creek fleeing her own scandal and found belonging in being useful and unseen. She realizes the redactions in Voss's file protect someone powerful — and that she has been the town's confessor without ever being its citizen. Beat: belonging questioned.

chapters.title: The Sixth Return
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The sixth return trip's destination is the municipal annex, where records are stored. Ada breaks in and finds Voss's original, unredacted file hidden in the archive: the predicted victim is Councilman Dale Petrossian, and the murder date hasn't passed yet. Beat: the clock restarts, stakes sharpen.

chapters.title: Petrossian's Ledger
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes investigates Petrossian and finds he signed off on Voss's firing and on burying a twelve-year-old hit-and-run — the same night of the rides in Ada's earliest logs. Beat: the past surfacing; the corruption is older and wider than one murder.

chapters.title: Someone Who Knows My Voice
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The killer calls the dispatch line, using a voice modulator, quoting Ada's own logged phrases back to her — proof he's studied her for years. He offers her a choice: stay silent and be safe, or keep digging and become the next entry. Beat: fear weaponized; Ada's isolation made explicit.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Tuesdays
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She audits her own archive and finds the killer's pattern requires a driver — someone who worked every Tuesday night shift. Only three drivers qualify; one, Tomás Iriarte, left the company the same week Voss was fired. Beat: the suspect list narrows; paranoia enters the depot.

chapters.title: The Farewell Booking
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A booking arrives under Voss's name — impossible, since he's dead — scheduling a ride for Petrossian on Thursday night. The killer is taunting her, or using Voss's credentials. Ada realizes he's inside the dispatch system itself. Beat: violation deepens; nowhere is neutral.

chapters.title: Tomás
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada confronts Tomás, now a school bus driver, and finds him terrified but innocent — he was Voss's informant inside the company, and Voss's death has him next on the list. He gives her Voss's notebook. Beat: an ally gained; tenderness flickering between two frightened people.

chapters.title: The Notebook
chapters.summary: Ada and Reyes's POV alternating. Voss's notebook names his theory: the killer is protecting the twelve-year-old hit-and-run's true driver — someone whose identity the council buried. Reyes admits the case file was sealed from above. Beat: the institution itself is the accomplice; duty and love of the town collide.

chapters.title: Sealed From Above
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes's captain shuts down her inquiry and suspends her for 'improper contact with a witness.' She goes to Ada off the record. Beat: Reyes loses her badge's protection and gains a partner; the two women commit to each other over the institution.

chapters.title: Thursday Night
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada and Reyes set a trap: Petrossian is warned and 'taken' by police, but a decoy ride runs the scheduled route. The decoy cab is run off the road — the killer takes the bait but escapes when a second car intervenes. Beat: the trap half-works; the killer has help.

chapters.title: The Second Car
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada replays the night's radio traffic and catches a dispatcher's phrase she never logged — someone has been shadowing her shifts. The killer isn't a driver at all: he's the day dispatcher, Roy Calloway, whose brother drove the car in the original hit-and-run. Beat: the reveal inverts her world; her own office was the nest.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada finds a new page added to the file in her own handwriting style: the final entry names her, scheduled for Sunday night. Calloway calls to say he only ever wanted his brother's name cleared and the town's lie kept — and that Ada, the keeper of records, is the last person who could expose it. Beat: the killer's twisted logic laid bare; Ada's choice crystallizes.

chapters.title: What Ada Would Do
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada refuses to run. She and Reyes stage the archive: they 'restore' the sealed hit-and-run file and broadcast its contents on the dispatch channel, forcing Calloway to come to the depot to destroy the master logs. Beat: courage as authorship — Ada decides what the record will say.

chapters.title: Night Shift
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, climax. Sunday night, the depot becomes the trap. Calloway comes with the fire of a true believer; in the struggle Ada uses her encyclopedic knowledge of the building and the radio system against him, and Reyes takes him down as he tries to burn the logs. Beat: fear transfigured into mastery; the keeper of records becomes the record.

chapters.title: The Whole File
chapters.summary: Reyes and Ada's POV. The sealed hit-and-run becomes public; Petrossian resigns, the captain is investigated, and Tomás is cleared. Ada testifies, naming everything she kept filed away for twelve years, including her own silences. Beat: cost and catharsis; belonging earned through truth, not usefulness.

chapters.title: A Letter for the Witness
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, resolution. Weeks later, Ada finds a letter Voss mailed before dying, thanking the dispatcher he never met for being the one person who would read the file to the end. Ada pins it above her board, takes the day dispatcher's chair, and answers the first call of her new shift. Beat: quiet peace; the town's secrets now have a witness, not a keeper.
